synopsis: ASAM OSI is an open, free messaging standard connecting environment, sensor, fusion and function models; its messages include timestamped ground truth, sensor views, sensor data and detected objects [f9214, f9217, f5260, f13219]. Across the booklet, OSI supports tool-chain integration, semantic replay and branching into closed-loop simulation, while providing a pattern for defining detected objects, warnings and brake requests before hardware selection [f8714, f13464, f5540, f13228]. OSI-compatible sensor models can transfer between simulators and be supplied as sealed intellectual-property-protecting packages; the booklet recommends OSI/OSMP FMUs using FMI 2.0 when suppliers withhold internals [f13220, f13221, f4857]. Although the glossary rates OSI and FMI as domain-neutral and transferable to off-road work, the cited OSI evidence has road-vehicle origins, so quarry deployment remains an engineering adaptation rather than off-road proof [f13224, f5507, f5262]. High-fidelity sensor extensions run from April 2025 to March 2027, leaving interface-versioning risk while the validation program integrates its first tool chain; export capabilities and ownership-change exit clauses are recommended to limit supplier dependence [f8618, f13227, f8619, f8733, f8887].
